name: Question 20
problem:
Given that

$$
\frac{1+3x}{(x-1)(x+1)^{3}}=\frac{A}{x-1}+\frac{B}{x+1}+\frac{C}{(x+1)^{2}}+\frac{D}{(x+1)^{3}},
$$

where $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ are real constants, find the value of $AB-CD.$
worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x-1)(x+1)^{3}$ gives

$$
1+3x=A(x+1)^{3}+B(x-1)(x+1)^{2}+C(x-1)(x+1)+D(x-1).
$$

Letting $x=-1$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1+3(-1) & =A(-1+1)^{3}+B(-1-1)(-1+1)^{2}+C(-1-1)(-1+1)+D(-1-1) \\ 1-3 & =-2D \\ -2 & =-2D \\ D & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=1$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1+3(1) & =A(1+1)^{3}+B(1-1)(1+1)^{2}+C(1-1)(1+1)+D(1-1) \\ 1+3 & =8A \\ 4 & =8A \\ A & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=0$ and using our values for $A$ and $D$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1+3(0) & =\frac{1}{2}(0+1)^{3}+B(0-1)(0+1)^{2}+C(0-1)(0+1)+1(0-1) \\ 1 & =\frac{1}{2}-B-C-1 \\ C & =-\frac{3}{2}-B.\,\,(1)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, letting $x=2$ and using our values for $A$ and $D$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1+3(2) & =\frac{1}{2}(2+1)^{3}+B(2-1)(2+1)^{2}+C(2-1)(2+1)+1(2-1) \\ 1+6 & =\frac{27}{2}+9B+3C+1 \\ 3C & =-\frac{15}{2}-9B \\ C & =-\frac{5}{2}-3B.\,\,(2)\end{aligned}
$$

From $(1)$ and $(2)$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2}-B & =-\frac{5}{2}-3B \\ 2B & =-1 \\ B & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute the value of $B$ into $(1)$  to get the value of $C:$

$$
C=-\frac{3}{2}-(-\frac{1}{2})=-1
$$

Finally,

$$
AB-CD=\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{2})-(-1)(1)=\frac{3}{4}.
$$

Question 20

Given that 1+3x(x−1)(x+1)3=Ax−1+Bx+1+C(x+1)2+D(x+1)3, where A, B, C and D are real constants, find the value of AB−CD.

a
12
b
4
c
14
d
34
e
2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Multiplying both sides of the given equality by (x−1)(x+1)3 gives 1+3x=A(x+1)3+B(x−1)(x+1)2+C(x−1)(x+1)+D(x−1).

Letting x=−1 gives 1+3(−1)=A(−1+1)3+B(−1−1)(−1+1)2+C(−1−1)(−1+1)+D(−1−1)1−3=−2D−2=−2DD=1.

Letting x=1 gives 1+3(1)=A(1+1)3+B(1−1)(1+1)2+C(1−1)(1+1)+D(1−1)1+3=8A4=8AA=12.

Letting x=0 and using our values for A and D gives 1+3(0)=12(0+1)3+B(0−1)(0+1)2+C(0−1)(0+1)+1(0−1)1=12−B−C−1C=−32−B.(1)

Now, letting x=2 and using our values for A and D gives 1+3(2)=12(2+1)3+B(2−1)(2+1)2+C(2−1)(2+1)+1(2−1)1+6=272+9B+3C+13C=−152−9BC=−52−3B.(2)

From (1) and (2) we have −32−B=−52−3B2B=−1B=−12.

Now we substitute the value of B into (1) to get the value of C: C=−32−(−12)=−1

Finally, AB−CD=12(−12)−(−1)(1)=34.
